colors.role: secondary CTA fill (Member Login), counter numerals

taste.name: Walls of colour instead of dividers
taste.trigger: When separating 14 stacked topics on one long scroll
taste.decision: Chose full-width hard ground changes (white, lavender gradient, indigo gradient) with 0px gaps over whitespace-and-rule separation on a single ground
taste.reason: Because a reader skimming at speed registers a colour change before a heading, so each switch is a free chapter marker
evidence: lavender three sections in a row and indigo two in a row, where the marker stops working

taste.name: Conversion green, fenced off
taste.trigger: When deciding where the second brand colour goes
taste.decision: Chose to confine green to Get Started, Member Login and counter numerals over spreading it across headings, icons or grounds
taste.reason: Because a colour that only ever means act here is found without reading; the cost they accepted is a white label at 1.94:1 on #3BD633
evidence: #2F3292 carries headings and nav (39 text uses)

taste.name: One typeface, no instrument voice
taste.trigger: When a vehicle-tracking company chose its type system
taste.decision: Chose Cabin alone in three weights over pairing a text face with a monospaced or technical face for data
taste.reason: Because one rounded sans reads as approachable to non-technical fleet buyers, at the price of never sounding like instrumentation
evidence: 0 monospaced elements, including on counter and dashboard figures

taste.name: Liveness through perpetual motion
taste.trigger: When the page had to feel live, like the tracking product
taste.decision: Chose infinite ambient keyframes and six autoplay carousels over motion that responds only to the reader
taste.reason: Because constant movement tells a first-time visitor real-time in the first second, before any copy is read
evidence: pulse, location-pulse, dot-travel, gpsMove, moveDots, satellite-float and signal-pulse among 30+ keyframes
